rationale: Amended: raised the distances (week 1 30→36 km, week 2 37→44, week 3 42→49) and noted Friday's party. You said the distances were too cautious and your physio agrees. Her rule (run, stop above 3/10) already replaced my 0/10 gate, and she has seen the calf — I haven't — so her view outranks my cap. What I have not done: chase the curve. Two clean runs is a thin base, and the 14 Nov pattern (added 4 km, felt three days later) is why the steps stay modest: week 1 is ~14% over the 31.5 km ramp cap, not far beyond it, and the long run stays at 8 until the calf has had a normal week. Running very easy and judging on feel is the right method; keep paces 5:15/km or slower, no strides. Xmas party: Friday is rest, and a Saturday HRV dip after alcohol is an explained confounder that resolves in a day or two — it does not cut Saturday's easy run. Weeks 2 and 3 are provisional and rise only if this week is calf 0–1.
